sections.html: Currently available are flounder whiptail catfish from Peru, 10-13 cm long. These sizes give only the body length, as in Planiloricaria there is a filament on the upper lobe of the caudal fin that is as long as the body. The maximum length given in literature is 35 cm.
Offer them fine sand as substrate in the aquarium, so that the fish are able to bury themselves completely.
These fish feed basically on meat. They love mosquito larvae, bloodworm, daphnia etc., but also accept dry food (flakes, granules).

These whiptail catfish normally do not swim, but "walk" with their ventral fins. They are somewhat stiff and need large tanks that leave a lot of free space at the bottom. Towards conspecifics of similar size Planiloricaria are usually peaceful, but smaller specimens are often mobbed. Fish of other species are simply ignored. These catfish should never be kept together with fin-nibbling species, as the long fin filaments of Planiloricaria would certainly be damaged.
The sexes can be distinguished even in half-grown fish. The ventral fins in males are longer and more pointed than those of the females.
Planiloricaria: Latin, means "flat Loricaria"; Loricaria is another genus of catfish. cryptodon: from ancient Greek, means "with a hidden tooth".
